key_insight: Better visual AI requires access to the right evidence, not just more time to reason. A controlled study across 22 benchmarks found that increasing the base model’s inference budget delivered only modest gains.
problem_solved: Visual tasks often require grounded perception, external knowledge, and numerical measurements that a model cannot reliably obtain through internal reasoning alone.
method: Evaluate the benefits of increasing inference budgets across 22 benchmarks.
Use heterogeneous tools to obtain task-relevant visual evidence, external information, and measurements.
The title and partial abstract indicate an approach combining interpretable tool outputs with multimodal memory; implementation details are not provided.
impact: For practitioners, the findings suggest prioritizing evidence-gathering tools alongside reasoning compute. Tool integration and multimodal memory may help visual agents retain and use information needed for real-world tasks.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram: visual question → tool selection → evidence collection → multimodal memory → answer.
Qualitative comparison panel: more inference compute alone produces modest gains across 22 benchmarks.
Three evidence icons: grounded perception, external knowledge, and numerical measurement.
Memory-board illustration connecting images, tool outputs, and retained findings.
paper_title: OpenVLHarness: Real World Visual Agentic Tool-Use with Multimodal Memory
paper_authors: Yu Zhou, Cheng-Fu Yang, Rui Sun, Di Wu, Sibo Peng
